title: Tenant‑agnostic zero‑downtime orchestrator with health‑fencing and circuit rollback
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Private (VPC) customers require automated runtime/data‑plane upgrades that guarantee no visible downtime and deterministic rollback when health regressions occur. Current rollout controllers are tenant‑aware but we lack a tenant‑agnostic orchestration layer that enforces health fences and can perform accelerated circuit-style rollbacks when compound failures are detected.

Goal: Implement an orchestrator for private data‑plane runtime rollouts that: 1) performs tenant-agnostic staged upgrades (slice-based), 2) enforces strict health fences at each stage (synthetic and real traffic checks), 3) supports configurable drain/priming windows and KV prewarm hooks, 4) exposes a circuit-breaker rollback mode that immediately halts and reverts remaining stages when a health fence is tripped, and 5) integrates with Terraform/IaC toggles so operators can declare safe rollouts in code.

Proposed design summary:
- Controller: new "fence-controller" running as an operator in the private control plane. It loads rollout manifests (tenant slices, resource constraints, prewarm hooks) from the existing rollout API.
- Stage model: upgrade stages are defined by tenant-slice and slot groups. Each stage goes through: drain -> evac-priming -> apply -> synthetic health probes -> real-traffic sampling -> promotion.
- Health fences: two layers — synthetic probe assertions (latency, 5xx rate, KV hit patterns) and production sampling (p99 latency, error trend). Both must pass thresholds configured per rollout.
- Circuit rollback: if a fence trips, controller flips to "circuit-rollback" which: stops further stages, triggers fast rollback on affected slices, notifies routing to route around problematic slots, and escalates to oncall.
- Terraform integration: IaC module exposes rollout_definition resource, with toggles: max_concurrent_stages, priming_window_sec, synthetic_probe_profile, rollback_mode. Operators can use module to embed safety policy in PR.
- Observability: add per-rollout timelines in Console, event stream (start/finish/fence_trip/rollback), and detailed per-stage telemetry to trace which metrics caused the fence to trip.

Acceptance criteria:
- New fence-controller deployed to staging private control plane; can execute a sample rollout manifest with at least 5 stages.
- Synthetic probe failure and production sampling failure both trigger fence_trip events and start circuit rollback flow.
- Terraform module shipped and documented; can create rollout_definition and kick a rollout via CI.
- Console shows per-rollout timeline and links to implicated metrics and PRs.
- Rollback completes and system returns to pre-rollout state with no session loss beyond configured drain window for 99% of sessions.

Success metrics:
- Zero customer-facing downtime during 95% of staged rollouts in staging and canaries.
- Mean time to rollback from fence_trip < 2 minutes for fast rollback path.
- Number of manual rollbacks reduced by >= 70% for private upgrades after rollout of this feature.

Non-goals:
- Not attempting to replace tenant-specific evacuation logic in the runtime; this orchestrator coordinates and invokes existing evacuation APIs.
- Not handling database migrations or schema changes in this ticket — only runtime/data-plane binaries and configuration swaps.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- Controller scaffolding: CRD, controller runtime, reconciler loop (ENG-578451-T1).
- Stage workflow: drain primitives, priming hook runner, apply step, probe runner (ENG-578451-T2).
- Circuit rollback engine: fast-path rollback, routing isolation hook, oncall notifier (ENG-578451-T3).
- Terraform module: rollout_definition resource, examples and policy templates (ENG-578451-T4).
- Observability: event stream, console timeline UI hooks, and SLO annotations (ENG-578451-T5).
- E2E tests: synthetic failure injection harness and performance regression suite (ENG-578451-T6).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: aggressive fast rollback could cause cache/churn that temporarily spikes latency. Mitigation: add rate‑limit to rollback API and allow configurable backoff.
- Risk: false positives from synthetic probes due to environmental flakiness. Mitigation: require both synthetic+production sampling to fail for high‑confidence circuit trips by default; make this configurable.
- Risk: operator misconfiguration in Terraform could block rollouts. Mitigation: provide a validation webhook and a dry-run mode in CI.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype controller in staging with manual rollout manifests (week 1).
2) Add Terraform module and CI dry-run (week 2).
3) Run canary rollouts on internal non-customer slices with synthetic failure injection (week 3).
4) Open private beta for select customers with extra telemetry and runbook (week 4).
5) Gradual ramp to GA after 3 successful beta rollouts and postmortem review (week 6).

Rollback playbook (executive summary):
- Automatic: fence_controller receives failed fence -> flips to circuit-rollback -> triggers per-slice rollback plan -> notifies ops channel and console.
- Fast manual: oncall triggers rollback endpoint with target slice list -> controller verifies rollback safety and executes with preconfigured rate limits.
- Recovery: after rollback completes, controller runs a verification sweep (synthetic + production) and marks rollout as aborted with attached root cause.

Files/PRs/Artifacts:
- Design doc draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/private-rollout-fence (prototype link)
- Terraform module sketch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/212 (WIP)
- Controller PoC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-controller/pull/88 (draft)
- E2E harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-harness/tree/fence-poc

Next steps:

- Finalize CRD fields and Terraform schema (target 2026-02-17).
- Kick off ENG-578451-T1 and ENG-578451-T4 in the next sprint.
